seal.checks.title: Checks on the file
seal.checks.what: The signed PDF carries a digital seal made with the certificate of {name}. PDF readers show if the file changed after signing.
seal.checks.not: It is a seal of the server that made the file, not a signature of the people who signed.
seal.checks.more: What a PDF reader says about the seal
seal.time.stamp: It carries a trusted time stamp.
seal.time.stamp_unchecked: It carries a time stamp from a time-stamp service. This server was not set up to check whose service that is.
seal.time.clock: The time in it is this server's clock.
seal.ltv.on: Can be checked for years: the file carries what a PDF reader needs to check the seal after its certificate expires.
seal.ltv.missing: Can be checked only while the seal's certificate is valid. The services that confirm that certificate could not be asked, or did not answer in time. Nothing else is affected, and there is nothing you need to do.
seal.record.holds: Time-stamped by {name} on {time}, when everyone had finished.
seal.record.unchecked: Time-stamped by {name} on {time}, when everyone had finished. Who runs that service was not checked.
seal.record.changed: The history no longer matches the time stamp taken when everyone finished. Download the full record before you rely on it.
seal.record.missing: The history up to completion could not be time-stamped. The fingerprint printed on the certificate of completion still guards it.
seal.status.name: Digital seal (PAdES)
seal.status.on: PDF readers show if the file changed after signing. Every document completed from now on is sealed by {name}, with a certificate issued by {issuer}. Documents completed earlier stay as they are.
seal.status.until: The certificate ends on {day}. The people who run this server renew it.
seal.status.off: Not being applied right now, so documents completed now are made without it. Nothing else stops. The people who run this server have been told why.
pdfa.setting.title: Archive format (PDF/A)
pdfa.setting.hint: Make completed files PDF/A, an archive format some archives require, when the file allows it. Each document says whether it is, under Checks on the file. Files completed earlier stay as they are.
pdfa.setting.gone: This server can no longer check files, so documents completed now are made as normal PDFs. Tell whoever runs GrowSigning for you. You can switch this off.
pdfa.setting.trouble: The last check could not be done ({why}), so that document is not PDF/A. Tell whoever runs GrowSigning for you if it happens again.
pdfa.next.font: Next time, save the file as PDF/A in the program that made it (in Word: Save as, PDF, Options, PDF/A), then send it.
pdfa.next.cmyk: Next time, save the file as PDF/A, or with colours for screens (RGB), in the program that made it, then send it.
pdfa.next.media: Next time, send the file without sound, video, 3D or attached files.
pdfa.next.attached: If your archive needs PDF/A, ask signers to attach PDF/A files or photos.
pdfa.next.failed: Saving the file as PDF/A in the program that made it, then sending it, often helps. If it keeps happening, tell whoever runs GrowSigning for you.
pdfa.next.server: This is about the server, not your file. Documents completed later are checked as usual. If it keeps happening, tell whoever runs GrowSigning for you.

rules.title: Sign-in rules
rules.intro: What everyone on {account} needs to sign in. With nothing set here, each person chooses for themselves.
rules.load_failed: We could not load the sign-in rules. Reload the page to try again.
rules.password.label: Shortest password
rules.password.hint: From {lo} to {hi}. It applies when someone chooses a password. Someone whose password is shorter is asked for a longer one the next time they sign in with it.
rules.idle.label: Sign out after
rules.idle.minutes: {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} of no use
rules.idle.hours: {count, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} of no use
rules.idle.hint: Two minutes before, the page says so and offers "Stay signed in". Signing pages of your documents check their link again after a break this long.
rules.one.label: One session at a time
rules.one.hint: When someone arrives in {account} in another browser, the browser they used before is signed out of it. API keys are not affected.
rules.one.confirm: Switching this on now signs out every extra browser of people who are signed in to {account} more than once. This browser stays signed in.
rules.two_step.on: Two-step login is asked of everyone.
rules.two_step.off: Two-step login is each person's own choice.
rules.leak.on: New passwords that have appeared in a data leak are refused.
rules.why.summary: Why there is no forced password change and no rule about capitals or digits
rules.why.body: NIST, the standards body of the United States, advises against both (SP 800-63B). People who must change a password every few weeks, or fit one to a pattern, choose weaker ones and write them down. A longer password, the check against leaked passwords and two-step login do more.
rules.code.label: Your code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code
rules.saved_out: Saved. {count, plural, one {# other browser was} other {# other browsers were}} signed out.
rules.owner_short: Your own password is shorter than {min} characters. As the owner you are not held by this rule, but choose a longer one under "Your sign-in" above.
rules.refused.password: Shortest password: type a whole number from {lo} to {hi}. It is still {kept}.
rules.refused.idle: Sign out after: choose a time from {lo} to {hi} minutes, or Never. It is still {kept}.
rules.password.too_short: Use a password of at least {min} characters.
rules.password.too_short_team: Use a password of at least {min} characters. {account} asks that of everyone on its team.
rules.password.leaked: This password has appeared in a data leak. Choose another one.
rules.password.gate: {account} asks everyone on the team for a password of at least {min} characters, and yours is shorter. Choose a longer one first. Until then nothing else in {account} opens for you. Your other workspaces are not affected.
rules.short.title: Choose a longer password to open {account}
rules.short.body: {account} asks everyone on the team for a password of at least {min} characters, and the one you signed in with is shorter. Choose a new one here and you carry on at once. Nothing was lost.
rules.short.forgot: Signed in another way and do not know the password? Sign out and use "Forgot password" on the sign-in page.
rules.short.failed: We could not save this, and nothing was changed. Check your connection and try again.
rules.warn.text: You will be signed out in {left}, because {account} signs out a browser that is not used for {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
rules.warn.failed: We could not reach the server, so we could not keep you signed in. Check your connection and press it again.
rules.left.minutes: about {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
rules.out.idle: You were signed out because this browser was not used for a while. That is a rule of your team. Sign in to carry on where you were.
rules.out.elsewhere: You were signed out here because you signed in on another browser, and your team allows one session at a time. Sign in here to use this browser instead.
rules.away.checked: You were away for a while, so we checked the link again.

sign.error.unknown_link: We do not recognise this link. It may have been copied incompletely.
sign.error.turn_not_yet: It is not your turn yet.

sign.error.access_code_wait: That makes {tries} wrong codes from your internet connection in a quarter of an hour. Wait {minutes} minutes and try again, or ask {sender} for the code: {email}. Nothing you filled in is lost.

sign.supplements.failed: We could not save that. Check your connection and tick it again.
sign.supplements.open_must: Open {name}, you must open it before you finish
sign.error.code_first: This document asks for a one-time code first. Type it, and the reminders stop straight after.
sign.error.code_not_needed: This document is already open on this device, so there is no code to wait for.
sign.error.consent_first: Please agree to use electronic records and signatures first.
sign.error.stamp_signers_only: Only someone who signs can put a stamp on this document.
sign.error.stamp_field_gone: That stamp field is not yours, or is no longer on the document. Load the page again to see it as it is now.
sign.error.stamp_before_gone: The stamp you put on before is not on the document any more. Choose a picture of the stamp again.
sign.error.stamp_saved_in_person: Saved stamps are not offered on a device that is handed to someone to sign in person. Upload a picture of the stamp or take a photo of it instead.
sign.error.stamp_saved_other_account: Saved stamps come from the account you are signed in to, and only when it is signed in with the address this document was sent to ({email}). Upload a picture of the stamp or take a photo of it instead.
sign.error.stamp_saved_gone: That stamp is not in your account any more. Someone on your team may have changed or deleted it. Choose another one.
sign.error.stamp_wait: That is a lot of stamp pictures in one hour, so this one was not taken. Wait {minutes} minutes and try again. A stamp that is already on the page stays there.
sign.error.stamp_not_yours: That stamp is not on your part of this document.
sign.error.comment_empty: Type your question or comment first. Nothing was sent.
sign.error.comment_too_long: A comment can be up to {max} characters, and this one has {length}. Make it shorter or split it in two. Nothing was sent.
sign.error.comment_limit: You have written {max} comments on this document, which is as many as one person can. Nothing was sent. If there is more to say, email {reach}.
sign.error.comment_burst: That is {count} comments in {window} minutes, which is as many as we take in that time. Nothing was sent. Wait {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} and send it again: what you typed is still in the box.
sign.error.not_your_turn: It is not your turn yet, so this document and its comments are not open to you yet. We will email you when it is. To reach {reach} before that, reply to the email you got from us.
sign.error.closed: This document is closed, so its comments are closed too. {sender} still has them.
sign.error.read_only: Everyone has finished, so the comments on this document can be read but no longer added to. To reach {reach}, write to them directly.
sign.error.thread_gone_unsent: That conversation is not on this document. Load the page again to see the ones you can read. Nothing was sent.
sign.error.thread_gone: That conversation is not on this document. Load the page again to see the ones you can read.
sign.error.form_everyone_thread: On a public form, what you write here goes to {sender} only, and everyone on the document reads this conversation. Ask {sender} in a question of your own instead. Nothing was sent.
sign.error.form_everyone: On a public form, what you write here goes to {sender} only. Send it to them instead. Nothing was sent.
sign.error.handed_on: This is the signing page of {name}, and this device has been handed to someone else since. So {name}'s private questions are not shown here, and nothing can be written here in their name. What is written for everyone is still shown. If you are {name}, ask {sender} to open your page for you again with "Host signing now".
sign.error.handed_on_unsent: This is the signing page of {name}, and this device has been handed to someone else since. If you are {name}, ask {sender} to open your page for you again with "Host signing now". Nothing was sent.
sign.error.settle_not_yours: Only the person who started this conversation, or the sender, can mark it as settled. You can still answer in it.
sign.delegate.for: Signing for {name}, who named you while they are away.
sign.delegate.take_on: If you continue, you sign for {name} with your own name and signature. {name} is told. If you should not, do nothing.
sign.delegate.person_note: {name} can also sign this for you. If you continue, you sign it yourself and {name} no longer can.
sign.delegate.removed_title: You no longer need to act on this
sign.delegate.removed: This no longer needs you to act for {name}. There is nothing for you to do.
sign.delegate.taken: {name} started on this themselves, or it is closed, so there is nothing for you to do.
sign.delegate.by: {name} agreed to sign this for you, as the person you named while you are away. So this link no longer opens the document. If that is wrong, contact {sender}.
sign.delegate.by_done: {name} finished this for you, with their own name and signature. If you need a copy, ask {sender}.
sign.delegate.by_declined: {name} declined this for you, so it is closed. If that is not what you wanted, contact {sender}.

sign.consent.tick_first: Tick the box above to agree, then choose Continue.
sign.error.ours: Something went wrong on our side.

starters.place_none: Not written for any one country.
starters.made_before: You made a template from this on {date}.

starters.roles: Who fills it in: {roles}. You add their names and email addresses when you send it.

starters.made: Template made. Read it through, then use it from Templates.

sign.handback.title: Thank you, {signer}. Please hand this device back to {sender}.
sign.handback.body: You have finished signing. This device belongs to {sender}, and there is nothing more for you to do on it.
sign.handback.note: For {sender} only. The account is locked on this device and asks for {sender}'s password before it opens.
sign.read.title: How to read the document
sign.read.about: Easy reading puts the words in one column, like a web page, with your fields where they sit. What you sign is the pages.
sign.read.skip: The pages below are pictures. Read the document in Easy reading instead
sign.read.banner: A reading aid. What you sign is the pages of the document.
sign.read.see_where: See this on the page, page {page}
sign.read.hidden: Some words in this page's file do not show on the page, such as white text. Easy reading leaves them out. To know what they are, ask {sender}.
sign.read.folded: Folded: about {words} words. Your fields in this part stay below.
sign.read.here: For you to fill in here
sign.read.table: Table, {rows} rows. Each row is read across.
handover.title: This device was handed to {signer} to sign
handover.lead: So that nobody reaches {name}'s account by accident, it is locked in this browser. Nothing was signed out anywhere else and nothing is lost.
handover.no_server: We could not reach the server, so nothing was checked. Check your connection and try again.
handover.no_password: This login has no password, because you sign in with Google or Microsoft. Sign in again that way to come back.
handover.covers: What this lock covers, and what it does not
handover.covers_body: It covers GrowSigning in this browser: no document, contact or setting of the account opens here until the password is typed. It does not cover:
handover.not_you: Not {name}? Please hand the device back to them.
mail.footer.not_sure: Not sure this email is real?
mail.footer.type_code: Type {address} into your browser and enter {code}.
mail.footer.never_ask: We never ask for a password or a payment by email.
mail.footer.button_link: If the button does not work, copy this link: {url}
mail.footer.cannot_open: Page will not open where you are? Reply to this email and ask {sender} to send the document as a PDF.
mail.footer.personal: The link is personal to you. Do not forward this email.
mail.footer.from_help: Sent by the people who answer help requests at GrowSigning.
mail.footer.no_paper: Signed digitally, so no paper, no printer and no courier.
mail.footer.trees: Sent with GrowSigning, where every dollar plants {trees} mangrove trees with Treegens.
mail.text.check: Not sure this email is real? Go to {url} and enter the security code {code}.
mail.text.report: Did not expect this, or does it look wrong? Report this email: {url}
mail.text.help: Need a hand with this document? {url}
mail.attach_missing: We could not attach {files} to this email: our stored copy could not be read when it went out, and the people who run this service have been told. Use the link in this email instead.
mail.request.heading.signer: {sender} sent you a document to sign
mail.request.heading.viewer: {sender} sent you a document to view
mail.request.heading.again.signed: {sender} changed this document after you signed it
mail.request.heading.again.approved: {sender} changed this document after you approved it
mail.request.heading.again.viewed: {sender} changed this document after you viewed it
mail.request.shared: More than one person on this document uses this email address. This link is for {name} only.
mail.request.again.signed: You signed "{subject}" on {when}. After that, {sender} changed the document, so what was signed then no longer counts. It is kept on record, and so is the change.
mail.request.again.approved: You approved "{subject}" on {when}. After that, {sender} changed the document, so what was approved then no longer counts. It is kept on record, and so is the change.
mail.request.again.viewed: You viewed "{subject}" on {when}. After that, {sender} changed the document, so what was viewed then no longer counts. It is kept on record, and so is the change.
mail.request.again.look.sign: Please look at the document again and sign again if you agree. Answers given the first time are still filled in to check. If you do not agree, you can decline or ask {sender} a question from the same page.
mail.request.again.look.approve: Please look at the document again and approve again if you agree. Answers given the first time are still filled in to check. If you do not agree, you can decline or ask {sender} a question from the same page.
mail.request.updated: {sender} changed this document after sending it. Please look at it again before you sign.
mail.request.reopened: {sender} gave everyone more time, so you can sign now.
mail.request.resumed: {sender} paused this document for a while and has now resumed it, so you can sign it again.
mail.request.expiring: This request closes on {when}. If you need longer, reply to this email and ask {sender} for more time.
mail.request.resent: You asked for a fresh link. Here it is.
mail.request.done.all.signed: You signed this document, and so has everyone else. The link opens the completed document, and you can download it there.
mail.request.done.all.approved: You approved this document, and so has everyone else. The link opens the completed document, and you can download it there.
mail.request.done.all.viewed: You viewed this document, and so has everyone else. The link opens the completed document, and you can download it there.
mail.request.done.wait.signed: You have already signed this document, so there is nothing more for you to do. The link opens it as it stands while the others finish.
mail.request.done.wait.approved: You have already approved this document, so there is nothing more for you to do. The link opens it as it stands while the others finish.
mail.request.done.wait.viewed: You have already viewed this document, so there is nothing more for you to do. The link opens it as it stands while the others finish.
mail.request.ready: You filled in everything, and what you filled in is saved. One step is left: open the document and press Finish. Until you do, it is not signed and {sender} has not received it.
mail.request.access_code: You will need an access code to open it. {sender} will give it to you separately. It is not in this email.
mail.request.trees: {count, plural, one {# mangrove} other {# mangroves}} will be planted with Treegens when you finish.
mail.request.reply: Reply to this email to reach {sender} ({email}).
mail.request.own_time: The signing page shows your own time.
mail.request.mute: Too many reminders? Stop them for this document: {url}

text.code: {code} is your GrowSigning code to open a document from {sender}. It works for {minutes} minutes. Did not ask for it? Ignore this text.
mail.code.subject: Your code to open a document from {sender}
mail.code.heading: {code} is your code
mail.code.type: Type this code on the page that asked for it. It works for {minutes} minutes, and only for the document {sender} sent you.
mail.code.never_ask: Nobody at GrowSigning and nobody working for {sender} will ever ask you for this code. If you did not just open a document from {sender}, someone else has the link that was emailed to you: do not pass the code on, and tell {sender} ({email}).
mail.code.never_ask_plain: Nobody at GrowSigning and nobody working for {sender} will ever ask you for this code. If you did not just open a document from {sender}, someone else has the link that was emailed to you: do not pass the code on.
sso.error.failed: {name} did not confirm who you are, so you are not signed in. Try again in a minute, and if it keeps happening, ask the people who run {name}.
sso.error.cancelled: You stopped at {name} before it was finished, so you are not signed in. Press the button again when you are ready.
sso.error.expired: That sign-in was used already, or it took longer than 10 minutes, so we stopped it to be safe. Start again from this page, and allow cookies from this site if it keeps happening.
sso.error.domain: {name} gave us an address that is not at one of your organisation's email domains, so you are not signed in. Ask the people who run {name} which address your login there has.
sso.error.off: We could not reach your organisation's sign-in just now, or it is no longer set up for this address, so nothing happened. Try again in a few minutes, or ask an admin of your team.
sso.error.busy: Too many attempts from here, so we paused sign-ins for a moment. Wait a few minutes and try again.
sso.error.no_email: {name} did not give us a confirmed email address for you, so you are not signed in. Ask the people who run {name} to share your email address with GrowSigning.
sso.error.taken: Another person at {name} is already connected to the GrowSigning login with this address, so you are not signed in. Ask the people who run {name} which of their logins should have your address.
sso.error.session: This browser is signed in to a different GrowSigning login than the one this sign-in was for, so nothing changed. Sign out or sign in again, then try once more.
sso.refused.password: {name} signs everyone at {domain} in through its own sign-in service, so a password does not open this login. Press "Continue with {name} sign-in" on the sign-in page.
sso.refused.signup: {name} signs everyone at {domain} in through its own sign-in service, so no login with a password is made for this address. Press "Continue with {name} sign-in" on the sign-in page, and your login is made there.
sso.refused.way_back_two_step: The owner's password is a way back in only while two-step login is on, so you are not signed in. Sign in with "Continue with {name} sign-in", then switch two-step login on under Settings, Security.
sso.refused.two_step_off: You own {account}, where everyone signs in through {name}, and your password with two-step login is the way back in if {name} ever breaks, so two-step login stays on and nothing was changed. Switch off "Everyone at these domains signs in through {name}" under Settings, Security first, or choose "Move to another app" to use another phone.
sso.refused.hand_over: Everyone at your domains signs in through {name}, and the owner's way back in, if it ever breaks, is their password with two-step login. {person} does not have two-step login on, so the account was not handed over. Ask them to switch it on under Settings, Security first.
sso.err.key: An API key cannot change single sign-on. Sign in to the app as an owner or admin and change it under Settings, Security.
sso.err.no_key: This server cannot keep a client secret safely, so single sign-on cannot be set up here. Ask the people who run this server to set FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
sso.err.domain_form: That is not a domain we can check, so nothing was added. Type it like {example}, without @ or a web address.
sso.err.domains_max: An account can claim at most {max} domains, so nothing was added. Remove one you no longer use first.
sso.err.domain_taken: {domain} is claimed by another GrowSigning account, so it was not added. Ask whoever runs your DNS which account that is, or write to us from Help.
sso.err.domain_gone: That domain is no longer on this account. Reload the page to see the domains it has now.
sso.err.use_form: Use for single sign-on is on or off, so nothing was changed. Send use_sso as true or false.
sso.err.issuer_none: Nothing answers at {host} right now, so nothing was saved. Check the issuer address with the people who run your sign-in service.
sso.err.issuer_private: {host} leads to {address}, which is inside a private network, so the issuer cannot be used and nothing was saved. Use the issuer address your sign-in service shows to the internet.
sso.err.issuer_closed: This server is set up for a closed network and does not look up {host}, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run this server to add {host} to OUTBOUND_ALLOW.
sso.err.issuer_later: We could not check where {host} leads just now, so nothing was saved. Try again in a minute.
sso.err.discovery_address: That issuer is not an https address, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service, like {example}.
sso.err.discovery_unreachable: We could not reach the issuer just now, so nothing was saved. Check the address and try again in a minute.
sso.err.discovery_not_openid: The issuer did not answer as an OpenID Connect service, so nothing was saved. Check that the address is the issuer, not the page where people sign in.
sso.err.discovery_issuer_differs: The service names a different issuer than the one you typed, so nothing was saved. Copy the issuer exactly as your sign-in service shows it.
sso.err.discovery_insecure: The service gives an address that is not https, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run it to use https for every address.
sso.err.discovery_no_pkce: The service does not offer PKCE with S256, which keeps sign-ins safe, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run it to switch it on.
sso.err.discovery_no_alg: The service signs its tokens in a way we do not accept, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run it to use RS256 or ES256.
sso.err.name_form: That name cannot be used, so nothing was saved. Give a name of 1 to {max} characters, like the name of your organisation.
sso.err.issuer_form: That issuer is not an https address, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service, like {example}.
sso.err.client_id_form: That client id cannot be used, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service, without spaces.
sso.err.secret_needed: A client secret is needed, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service.
sso.err.secret_form: That client secret is too long, so nothing was saved. Copy it again from your sign-in service.
sso.err.enforced_change: Everyone at your domains signs in through {name} now, so its issuer and client id cannot change, and nothing was saved. Switch that off first, change them, try a sign-in, then switch it on again.
sso.err.no_service: No sign-in service is set up for this account. Add one under Settings, Security, Single sign-on.
sso.err.switch_form: These switches are on or off, so nothing was changed. Send enforce and join_new as true or false.
sso.err.try_first: {name} has not been tried yet, so nothing was switched on. Press "Try a sign-in" first and sign in there.
sso.err.no_domain: None of your domains is shown to be yours and set to use single sign-on yet, so nothing was switched on. Add a domain and its DNS line first.
sso.err.owner_two_step_you: Your way back in, if the sign-in service ever breaks, is your password with two-step login, so nothing was switched on. Switch two-step login on under Your sign-in first.
sso.err.owner_two_step: The owner's way back in, if the sign-in service ever breaks, is their password with two-step login, so nothing was switched on. Ask the owner to switch two-step login on first.

sso.mail.lost.subject: Single sign-on paused for {domain}
sso.mail.lost.heading: Single sign-on is paused for {domain}
sso.mail.lost.line1: We could not find the DNS record {record} any more, so people at {domain} sign in to {account} the usual way until it is back.
sso.mail.lost.line2: Put the record back as it is shown under Settings, Security, Single sign-on, and press Check now. If you removed it on purpose, remove the domain there too.
sso.mail.connected.subject: {name} sign-in can now open your GrowSigning login
sso.mail.connected.heading: {name} sign-in was connected to your login
sso.mail.connected.line1: Your organisation showed that it runs {domain}, and {name} confirmed that {email} is yours, so signing in with {name} now opens this GrowSigning login.
sso.mail.connected.line2: If this was not you, tell the people who run {name} at your organisation, and write to us from Help.
sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.lead: Your team can sign in with your organisation's own login. Once everyone at your domains has to sign in through it, someone whose login there is closed is signed out here within {hours} hours. API keys they made keep working until you remove them from the team.
sso.standard: OpenID Connect: the standard your sign-in service uses.
sso.domains.title: Your email domains
sso.domains.lead: Show that a domain is yours with one line in its DNS. Single sign-on is then used for addresses at it.
sso.domains.label: Domain
sso.domains.lost: Its DNS line is gone, so single sign-on is paused for it. Put the line back and press Check now.
sso.domains.record: Add a TXT record with this name and value where the DNS of {domain} is kept:
sso.domains.not_found: We did not find the line yet. A new DNS line can take up to a day to show.
sso.domains.unknown: The DNS did not answer just now. Try again in a minute.
sso.domains.not_used: Single sign-on is not used for it. People there sign in the usual way.
sso.service.title: Your sign-in service
sso.service.name: Name people see
sso.service.name_hint: Shown on the sign-in button, like Acme.
sso.service.issuer_hint: The web address of your sign-in service, copied from its settings.
sso.service.client_id_hint: The name your sign-in service gave GrowSigning when you registered it.
sso.service.secret_hint: The password it gave GrowSigning. Kept encrypted.
sso.service.secret_kept: Kept encrypted. Leave it empty to keep the one saved.
sso.service.redirect: Paste this address into your sign-in service as the place to send people back to:
sso.service.untried: Nothing changes for your team until you try a sign-in once and it works.
sso.service.tried_now: The sign-in worked. People at your domains now see "Continue with {name} sign-in" on the sign-in page.
sso.service.removed: Single sign-on was removed. People at your domains sign in the usual way again.
sso.rules.enforce: Everyone at these domains signs in through {name}
sso.rules.enforce_hint: Passwords, Google and Microsoft stop working for them, and signed-in browsers end within {hours} hours. The owner's way back in, if the service breaks, is their password with two-step login.
sso.rules.join: Add people from these domains as members when they first sign in
sso.rules.owner_two_step: The owner needs two-step login on before this can be switched on.
sso.rules.owner_two_step_you: Switch two-step login on under Your sign-in first. It is your way back in if the sign-in service breaks.
sso.rules.no_way_back: The owner has no two-step login on now, so nobody has a way back in if {name} breaks. Ask the owner to switch two-step login on under Settings, Security.
sso.rules.no_way_back_you: You have no two-step login on now, so nobody has a way back in if {name} breaks. Switch two-step login on under Your sign-in.
